concerns.text: Task T002 is tagged `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it writes files into the `code/` directory that is created by T001. Implicit ordering is required: T001 must complete before T002 can succeed.
Task T005 is marked `[P]` yet it writes Python modules under `src/utils/`. Those directories are created by Phase 0 (T001). Therefore T005 depends on T001 and cannot be safely run in parallel.

Task T006 is `[P]` but it calls the deterministic question mapper which loads datasets downloaded by T003 and uses configuration utilities from T005. It therefore has hidden dependencies on T003 and T005, violating the parallel‑safety guarantee.
Task T007 is `[P]` yet it reads the raw datasets produced by T003. It must run after T003; the `[P]` tag incorrectly suggests it can execute concurrently.

Task T013 is `[P]` but it loads the three checkpoints generated by the training scripts (T012). It cannot be parallel‑safe with the training phase; the tag should be removed or the task reordered after T012.
Task T014 is `[P]` while it aggregates `metrics.json` files written by T013 for each seed. It depends on the completion of T013 and thus must not be marked parallel‑safe.
Task T015 is `[P]` yet it orchestrates the entire end‑to‑end pipeline, invoking all prior tasks. Its execution inherently requires the preceding tasks to have finished, so the `[P]` tag is invalid.
Task T016 is `[P]` but it runs `quickstart.sh`, which in turn calls `run_all.py` (T015). It therefore depends on T015 and cannot be parallel‑safe.
Task T017 is `[P]` but it validates JSONL files that are produced by T008, T009, and T007. It must run after those generation tasks; the parallel‑safe tag is incorrect.

Task T018 is `[P]` yet it tests timeout and OOM guards implemented in the training loop (T011) and trainer scripts (T012). It must be executed after those scripts exist and are runnable, so it should not be marked `[P]`.
